recommendations.name: Southwest Ridge Route
recommendations.summary: Keep this as the climb from the Swamp Creek side, reached by boat to Stehekin and the Agnes Creek trail, and rewrite the map pins, the day-by-day trip plan and the partner requirements, which currently describe a different approach through Holden Village.
recommendations.detail: The only documented ascent of Mount Lyall found goes up Agnes Creek to a camp at Swamp Creek, crosses Swamp Creek at about 3,600 ft, climbs into the broad basin below the peak, heads for the 7,300 ft notch on the southwest ridge, traverses below the white vertical rock strip and finishes up an exposed Class 3 gully and loose boulders, with some Class 4 moves. The row's name, beta, approach, approach_variants, climbing_route, pitch_detail, descent, bail and access fields all match that. The waypoints after the first one (Holden Village, the Holden Lake trail, the avalanche chutes, Holden Lake, the basin below Holden Pass), the first waypoint's note, and partner_requirements describe a Lucerne/Holden/Railroad Creek approach. No summer ascent of Lyall from that side was found: the one Holden Pass route page describes it as a winter/spring ski route only, because the north side is dense brush. The itinerary and timing text also call it a Class 2-3 'South Route' up south slopes through the 'Entiat' backcountry, which contradicts the Class 3-4 southwest ridge line and grade; it should be rewritten as a roughly 3-5 day Agnes Creek/Swamp Creek trip. Separately, the 2026 Sisi Fire closures shut this approach for now, but they are dated and the row already states them, so they do not change which approach is correct.

recommendations.name: Southeast Ridge
recommendations.summary: This page mixes two separate climbs on Argonaut. Rename this one the East Ridge and keep its detailed climbing description, then create a new Southeast Ridge page for the 8-pitch count, the rappels into the notch and the Southeast Ridge day plan.
recommendations.detail: Route guides list two distinct lines. The Southeast Ridge (II 5.6) runs 8 pitches to the southeast spire, a false summit, then continues to the true summit. It uses two single-rope rappels or one double-rope rappel into the notch, its lower pitches are blocky and lichen-covered, and the recommended approach is over Colchuck Col; the Ingalls Creek approach is called a long, strenuous bushwhack. The East Ridge starts from the Argonaut-Colchuck col and climbs blocky Class 4 to 5.6 ground through the black towers. It is also the line Northwest Arete parties descend, in four rappels to that col. This row's id, beta, the end of its approach (the notch west of the lone gendarme, '6 pitches'), its six-row pitch_detail and most of descent_text describe the East Ridge. Its name, face, aspect, pitches=8, rappels, overview, two of its obj_haz entries (the lichen-covered lower pitches and the SE spire route-finding) and its itinerary/timing ('8-pitch Southeast Ridge') describe the Southeast Ridge. No East Ridge row exists among the siblings, so both climbs deserve a page. When renaming, restore the four-rappel descent to the col, which an earlier fix removed from detailed_rack because it assumed the row was the Southeast Ridge. rappel_detail's 'snow ledge toward the east gully' belongs to the Northeast Couloir and should come off both. The Southeast Ridge page will need its beta and breakdown researched from scratch: the full route pages returned 403 here.

recommendations.name: Southeast Face (Standard)
recommendations.summary: Keep this as the standard South Peak climb from the Hozomeen campground by way of Hozomeen Lake, and redraw the map pins, which follow a different, much longer approach from the Lightning Creek landing and mark points on the neighbouring Southeast Buttress climb.
recommendations.detail: A trip report of this line ('southeast route via the south face') starts at the Hozomeen Lake trailhead by the campground, leaves the trail after about 1.5 mi at 2,400 ft, crosses Hozomeen Creek through devil's club into the basin, reaches the 6,800 ft saddle camp over red scree and slabs, and climbs a roughly 15 ft 5.6 headwall to the summit. The party made two rappels on the way down. The trip was 12 mi round trip from 1,720 ft to 8,003 ft. That is exactly what the row's approach, primary approach_variant, itinerary and descent say. The Hozomeen border gate is closed to vehicles and walkers, so the campground is reached by the Ross Lake water taxi, as the row says. The waypoints instead follow the Lightning Creek landing, Willow Lake and a Ross Dam trailhead, and place a 6,200 ft saddle and a 'crux chimney' on the southeast buttress, which belongs to the sibling Southeast Buttress (South Peak) route. They should be replaced with the Hozomeen campground/trailhead, the Hozomeen Lake outlet turn-off, the chockstone gully near 5,000 ft, the slab wall near 5,800 ft and the 6,800 ft saddle camp. By that report the trip is about 6 mi one way (about 9.7 km, not 12.9) and gains about 6,300 ft, matching the itinerary rather than gain_ft 6,800. A second report on a west-gully variant gives 15 mi and 7,500 ft, so these are medium confidence. The beta's 'most parties traverse the northeast ridge' does not describe this line and should be rewritten from the approach and descent text.

recommendations.name: West Ridge / Southwest Gully
recommendations.summary: Keep this as the climb from Easy Pass down into Fisher Creek and up the south basin, and rewrite the day-by-day trip plan and the opening description, which instead describe a high traverse along the ridge crest over Cub Peak.
recommendations.detail: Both approaches are real: one detailed report drops about 1,500 ft from Easy Pass into Fisher Creek, leaves the trail about half a mile past Fisher Camp and climbs the drainage to a 6,700 ft ridge-step bivy (16 mi and 8,200 ft round trip). Other parties traverse high from Easy Pass along or below the Ragged Ridge crest. No source calls either one the standard. The row's approach, waypoints, approach_variants, climbing_route, descent_text and baseFinding are all built on the Fisher Creek line, so the smallest honest fix is to keep it. The itinerary's day notes and schedules, timing.sectionBreakdown, and the overview's 'long, exposed cross-country traverse of the Ragged Ridge crest from Easy Pass' describe the crest traverse over the Kitling saddle and Cub Peak and should be rewritten to Fisher Creek. The crest traverse could stay as a second approach_variant. dist_km 24.1 is the round trip; one way is about 12-13 km (about 8 mi). The camp list's Wing Lake, Lewis Lake and Rainy Pass entries serve Black Peak, not this climb.

recommendations.name: Disappointment Peak Cleaver (Cool Glacier)
recommendations.summary: This is the same climb as the existing Cool Glacier / Gerdine Ridge page: combine them into one page, keeping this page's fuller approach, descent and trip-plan text, and drop the two map pins that sit on the far side of the mountain.
recommendations.detail: One climbing club calls this route the 'Disappointment Peak Cleaver', another guide calls it 'Disappointment Cleaver (Gerdine Ridge)' and a third calls it 'Gerdine Ridge/Cool Glacier'. All three describe one line: the North Fork Sauk trail to White Pass, across the White Chuck Glacier to Glacier Gap (about 7,250 ft), then north on the cleaver, either skirting Disappointment Peak on the Gerdine/Cool glaciers or going directly over it at Class 4, to the col and the summit. The sibling row wa_glacier_peak_cool_glacier_gerdine describes the same White Pass/Glacier Gap route, so the catalog lists one climb twice. Carry over this row's approach, approach_variants (with the Glacier Gap baseFinding), the direct-over-Disappointment variant in beta, descent_text and the corrected 4-day North Fork Sauk itinerary, and give the surviving page the name 'Disappointment Peak Cleaver (Gerdine Ridge / Cool Glacier)'. Do not carry over waypoints[1] 'Buck Creek Pass' or waypoints[2] 'Cool/Gerdine Basin Camp', which sit on the eastern approach. Settle gain_ft (9,846) against the itinerary's 8,450 on the merged page; published totals for this approach run about 9,000-9,200 ft.
